text:
Salutations arrivals crew,
The welfare officer mentioned a concern about clear signage just now, and I wanted to pass it on.

Please keep the intake route easy to read from the first point of contact through to handoff, and make sure every enclosure tag is placed where it can be seen without delay. The Companion Animal Travel Desk is relying on crisp, consistent guidance so that handlers do not waste steps or hesitate when a pet is moved. <<FACT F097>> The paperwork should stay with the crate at all stages, and any special comfort notes must be checked before the animal leaves the desk area.

We also need tighter discipline around the transfer path itself. Any temporary sign that is obscured, bent, or left in the wrong lane should be corrected at once, because confusion builds quickly when the flow is busy and the pet is unsettled. <<FACT F091>> If you see a mixed message between the desk note and the visible route markers, follow the desk note and alert the floor lead without delay. This is especially important for nervous animals, older pets, and cases where the handler has given a detailed care plan.

Please keep your tone calm with travelers, keep your instructions brief, and keep the route obvious for every team member who touches the case. Clear signs save time, reduce error, and help the animals settle faster. Thank you for the steady attention you give to this work.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
